items.caption:
Homemade Chick-fil-a :)

Chick-fil-a sauce

½ cup mayonnaise 
3 Tbsp barbecue sauce
2 Tbsp honey
2 Tbsp yellow mustard
½ Tsp kosher salt 
½ black pepper
½ a lemon juiced

Chicken Brine

4 boneless skinless chicken thighs 
1 cups buttermilk
1 cup pickle juice
1 Tbsp paprika
1 ½ Tbsp garlic powder
1 tsp cayenne
1 tsp white pepper
1 tsp onion powder
1 Tbsp kosher salt

Dry Drede 

2 cups all purpose flour
½ cup potato starch
1 Tbsp paprika
1 Tbsp garlic powder
1 tsp onion powder
1 tsp MSG (optional)
1 Tbsp kosher salt
2 ½ tsp cayenne 
1 tsp ground black pepper

Waffle Fries

3 large russet potatoes
1 ½ Tbsp white vinegar
1 Tbsp salt
1.5 qt vegetable oil for frying

Pickles

1 small english cucumber or ½ a large one, sliced into thin rounds 
1 Tbsp pickling spice
1 cup white vinegar
1 cup water
2 Tbsp sugar
1 tsp MSG optional 
2 Tbsp kosher salt
2 sprigs dill

Assembly 

4 burger buns
4 slices pepper jack 
1 small head butter lettuce,
1 beefsteak tomato, thinly sliced
Lemonade (for the traditional experience) 

For the Chick-fil-a sauce, in a mixing bowl add, mayonnaise, barbecue sauce, honey, yellow mustard, kosher salt, black pepper and lemon. Mix until fully combined and set aside in the fridge. 

For the pickles, add your sliced cucumber to your mason jar along with the dill and pickling spice. In your sauce pot add white vinegar, water, sugar, MSG and kosher salt. Bring to a simmer then pour into the mason jar. Screw the lid on, let cool then refrigerate while you prep everything else. 

Prep the fries. Peel your potatoes and cut on a slice once on a wavy  mandoline, quarter turn, slice again and so on and so forth to get your waffle fries. If you don't have a wavy mandoline, you can cut the potatoes normally.

Add the potatoes to a large bowl and cover with ice water. Mix well to remove the starch, drain and set aside. 

Fill a large pot ⅔ the way with water, cover with a lid and bring to a boil. Once boiling add, white vinegar and salt.
 
Add your fries carefully to the pot and cook for about 2-3 minutes until slightly soft but not fully cooked. When you break one in half it should not snap like it's raw but it should be cooked with slight resistance. Make sure not to over cook this. Remove your potatoes to a couple of wire racks to cool. 

Heat your frying oil in a large pot to 330°F.

Carefully add your fries in batches and fry for 1-2 minutes until par cooked but not golden. Remove to a wire rack and set aside while we work on our chicken.

Chicken Brine: To a large bowl add, buttermilk, pickle juice, kosher salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, cayenne and MSG. Add your chicken, mix well to coat and set aside in the fridge for 1 hour to overnight. Or use right away. 

In a large bowl add all purpose flour, potato starch, kosher salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, cayenne and whisk to combine. Remove the chicken from the fridge. Coat the chicken in the dry dredge with no bald spots then dip back in the wet brine then back in the dry with no bald spots. Place your coated chicken on a wire rack and set aside.

Heat your oil to 350° F. Once your oil is up to temp, fry your chicken, 2 pieces at a time for about 6-8 minutes, until fully cooked and golden brown and crispy. Remove to a wire rack and repeat with all your chicken. 

Heat your oil to 375°F. 

Carefully add your par cooked fries to the oil in batches and fry for 1-2 minutes until beautiful golden brown and crispy. Remove to a wire rack and season generously with salt. 

Assembly, on a toasted bun add sauce, pickles, lettuce, tomato, chicken and cheese. melt however possible then add the sauced top bun. Serve with the fries and lemonade. Enjoy!
